prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Scope: checked baggage, induction through screening, sorting, make-up to Outbound Load Control Desk handoff; airline loading excluded. Actors: Baggage Operations Supervisor, alias Tern (congestion/overload/recovery authorization, priority, make-up release, dispositions beyond operator authority; stops unsafe induction; uses Chute Occupancy Note; controls holds; holds/exceptions need owners). Security Duty Manager (alarm decisions, clears security holds, access control; checks Custody Seal Log). Explosives Response Team, alias Pebble (holds/exams, Custody Seal Log, communicates dispositions). Maintenance Technician (isolates energy, clears jams, uses Recovery Route Card, Calibration Witness Tag). Airline Ramp Coordinator (Carousel Release Slip to Carousel 7; reviews Bag Match Query mismatches before loading authorization; pre-loading verifies readable identity, current flight, permitting security disposition). Outbound Load Control Desk accepts loading record only if flight assignment, reconciled count, status consistent. Induction: Pier 4 Bag-Drop Unit (Oversize Exception Ticket to Image Resolution Desk); Bag Tag Printer (Calibration Witness Tag, replacement tags); Transfer Bag Feeder (Late Transfer Bag Card to Bag Reconciliation Station; accepts only verified identity/onward flight); Induction Tray Conveyor (meters valid bags). Control: Baggage Control System, alias Velvet (authoritative record; sort plans; receives Flight Cutoff Advisory; diverts to Secondary Inspection Chute; authorizes rejoin; reports missing/duplicate/delayed events). Concourse Zone Controller, alias Mosslight (induction permissive, Recovery Route Card, lanes; reports state/alarms to monitoring). Flight Data Gateway, alias Lantern (flight data, Flight Cutoff Advisory). Screening: North Gate Scanner, alias Kestrel, South Gate Scanner (Manual Rescan Receipt to Image Resolution Desk; fault holds feed). Image Resolution Desk records disposition. Bag Reconciliation Station (compares against expected flight population, flags missing/duplicates; Bag Match Query; mismatch holds). Primary Crossbelt Sorter, alias Juniper (Chute Occupancy Note). East/West Make-Up Conveyors (no bypass of identity checks, controlled access); Carousel 7 Make-Up Unit, alias Orchard. Requirements: hold bad/unscreened/unresolved bags; safe stop; custody controlled; count/identity differences block acceptance; departure-ready only after screening release, custody, reconciliation, loading checks recorded. Monitoring: throughput, availability, queues, scanner quality/alarms, desk backlog vs target, gateway timeliness/errors,

New part:
S238: The Transfer Bag Feeder is monitored for feed rate, interruptions, and backlog against its scheduled demand.
S239: The Carousel 7 Make-Up Unit is monitored for operating state, accumulation, and the time required to clear assigned work.
S240: The East Make-Up Conveyor and the West Make-Up Conveyor are assessed separately so that a local fault does not obscure the condition of the other conveyor.
S241: Tern reviews the operating dashboard and confirms that material service degradation has been assigned an owner and response priority.
S242: The Maintenance Technician investigates equipment faults that exceed the approved recovery interval and records the corrective action taken.
S243: The Security Duty Manager assesses any condition that could compromise screening coverage, security controls, or custody continuity.
S244: The Explosives Response Team is escalated to when an unresolved security condition requires its response under airport procedures.
S245: Service measures include availability, bags processed per operating interval, queue age, screening completion, and unresolved reconciliation differences.
S246: Thresholds and reporting intervals are established in the approved operating plan and reviewed against demand, flight schedules, and safety constraints.
S247: A degraded mode may be used only when the remaining equipment and procedures preserve required screening, traceability, custody, and reconciliation controls.
S248: Operations must suspend the affected activity when required controls cannot be maintained or when an unverified equipment state could misroute baggage.
S249: The Baggage Operations Supervisor coordinates escalation to maintenance, security, and airline operations according to the severity and operational impact of the condition.
S250: Return to service requires the fault to be corrected, required functional checks to pass, alarms to clear, and affected records to be reconciled.
S251: The responsible operational and technical personnel confirm that screening and custody controls are effective before normal routing resumes.
S252: The recovery is monitored at increased frequency until performance is stable and outstanding exceptions have been resolved or formally assigned.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
